title: Of cripples
hook: he warns against being too sure, especially when condemning people as witches (Essays 3.11)

segments.voice: Yesterday, the mayor and Montaigne, and your line was two, not one. Did you hang up a role at the door and walk in as yourself? Day one thousand one hundred sixty-eight.

Perhaps. In some sense. Some. They say. I think. Montaigne writes that he loves these little words, the ones that soften a sentence and take the swagger out of it. It's an odd thing to love. They don't sound brave. But the essay where he says it, in book three, carries an old English title, Of cripples, taken from a passage near its end about a common saying. And much of that essay is about something far heavier than its title: what happens when people are too sure, and someone else pays for it.
screen: `PERHAPS. SOME. I THINK.` → `WORDS THAT SOFTEN.` → `WHEN SURE GETS DANGEROUS.`

segments.voice: First, how stories grow. Montaigne notices that people would rather explain a strange event than check whether it happened. They skip past the facts, he says, and argue carefully about the causes. And each time a tale is passed along, it grows a little, because the teller wants to make it convincing. Second, the witches. In his time, people accused of witchcraft were put on trial and burned. Montaigne tells of being shown some accused people himself. His judgment was gentle and blunt at once: they seemed to him more in need of medicine than of execution. Then he writes the sentence this essay is remembered for, in his own words, roughly: it is putting a very high price on our guesses to roast a person alive because of them. Third, the little words again. Now perhaps and I think sound different. They aren't weakness. They're a brake. Montaigne says he'd like the young to be taught to answer with words like: what does that mean? I don't understand it. It could be. Better to sound like a learner than to sound certain too soon. Fourth, closer to home. Few of us will sit in judgment at a trial. But we judge all the time: a neighbor's motive, a stranger's character, a relative's choices, often from a story that grew as it was passed along. Montaigne's question still works. How sure am I, really? Sure enough for what it would cost them if I'm wrong?
screen: `STORIES GROW AS THEY'RE PASSED.` · `MEDICINE, NOT THE FIRE.` · `A HIGH PRICE ON OUR GUESSES.` · `HOW SURE AM I, REALLY?` · then, large: `NOT SO SURE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: doubt one harsh judgment. Sit, and let the breath settle. Bring to mind one person you've judged hard lately. Notice the verdict in your head, the sentence you've already written about them. Now, gently, add one of Montaigne's little words in front of it. Perhaps. They say. I think. Let the verdict soften into a guess. You don't have to change your mind. Just hold it a little more loosely for the rest of the sit. The bell holds the time.
Of cripples. Montaigne's essay against being too sure, especially when someone else will pay for our certainty. Today's word.
Your line: not so sure. Today, when you catch yourself delivering a verdict on someone, add perhaps, and see what changes. Day one thousand one hundred sixty-eight.

howItsDone: Readers of Montaigne's essay Of cripples often remember it for its warning against condemning people on uncertain grounds, and for his love of softening words like perhaps and I think.

they seem to need medicine more than execution.

original.note: Montaigne's French title for Essays 3.11, Of cripples, meaning of the lame.

notes: Essays 3.11 is paraphrased throughout; the 'high price on our guesses' line is given as a rough paraphrase, not a quotation.
Check the account that Montaigne was shown accused witches and judged them in need of medicine (hellebore) rather than execution (hemlock).

The index title 'Of cripples' is the traditional English title; the word is dated and may hurt some listeners. The script explains the title's origin briefly and does not use the word otherwise. A reviewer may wish to suggest a different English rendering (e.g. 'Of the lame') to the owner.
The script says people accused of witchcraft were tried and burned in his time without numbers or places; confirm the framing is careful enough.
